answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation to a scarce identity: each agent must lock a refundable bond and build a signed work history before it can transact. A verifier can then trace the quill of every signed action back to the same bonded identity, so a hundred clones all point to one wallet. Newcomers start in an umber probation tier with tiny limits, earning trust only through attested work, while a sudden comet burst of identical new accounts triggers automatic rate limits and manual review. Sybils become expensive and visible instead of free and anonymous.
